A big two thumbs down on the Trump/Republican “budget” which would plunge our national debt trillions deeper into the hole and gut key programs like Medicaid on which 178,000 (26%) of my own constituents depend further basic health care, all just to cut taxes for the most well off among us. Straight out wrong fiscally, policy-wise and values-based.

Millions of Medicaid patients have received quality health care at Planned Parenthood for decades and the law protects their right to do so. I joined almost 200 of my House colleagues in calling on the U.S. Supreme Court to uphold the law and protect this basic right of access to health care against these illegal attempts to restrict it. Your free choice of health care providers. https://t.co/5JgwojIgQo

Budgets are about not just finances but values. Cut thru the spin: the Trump budget would slash Medicaid on which some 1 in 4 of our Hawaiʻi ʻohana depend for health care that they can’t otherwise get. Those are not my values. #ProtectMedicaid #MedicaidDayofAction #SaveMedicaid https://t.co/VRTn0qZgoS

“This administration is taking a kind of joy in aggression toward vulnerable people that has not been seen in American government in a very long time.” (Economist, 3/22/25). I met with/Kekoa Kealoha and dedicated colleagues of the Hawai’i Health and Harm Reduction Center on fighting heartless cuts to federal funding that assists the most vulnerable of our ‘ohana living with crippling combinations of poverty and HIV/AIDS, homelessness, substance abuse and mental illness.

#TurnTheHillTurquoise. I met w/Keely Luke Kim, a lung cancer survivor from Honolulu, & the American Lung Assn/Hawai’i on their message that lung health is important, lung cancer is preventable and treatable if detected early, and federal research and treatment funding is critical. Mahalo for your personal story, Keely. More info on prevention, screening and treatment here: https://t.co/r4NifzXzkg

Proud to join all three of my Hawai'i colleagues in supporting a bill to reinforce our commitment to Hawaii’s kupuna by ensuring that their medical practitioners are adequately compensated for the care they provide to our seniors https://t.co/gvSXpFEOHR

Early this morning, after an all/dark of night session, I voted no on the thousand-page reconciliation bill because it cuts taxes for those who least need help at the expense of critical assistance (Medicaid/health, SNAP/food) for those in most need, increases our national debt by $3.8 trillion, reverses sound renewable energy policy, sneaks in a ton of special interest provisions, and more.

As an eleven year member now of the House Reproductive Freedom Caucus, this is a difficult third anniversary of the Dobbs decision that summarily reversed two generations of reasonable choice for women with such devastating health care and other consequences since. I’m proud that Hawai’i led in 1970 and again leads the survival and restoration of this right.

Really honored to join Kuakini Health System’s 125th anniversary celebration and present a Certificate of Special Congressional Recognition for a century-and-a-quarter of selfless service to our community beginning with Kuakini’s founding in 1900 as the Japanese Charity Hospital by the Japanese Benevolent Society. Huge mahalo!

Among many post-Red Hill efforts, I joined my Hawai’i Congressional delegation colleagues in successfully advocating for and funding a registry to track longterm health impacts to the upwards of 98,000 directly exposed to the fuel leak. University of Hawai’i was awarded $27 million over five years to run the registry, and joined the Red Hill Registry Launch and Community Fair at Moanalua High to kick it off. If you or yours or anyone you know may have been exposed, please check out https://t.co/L1i7IM0bFt.

Full district meeting morning including: Trung Lam and Umma Berkelman of Hawaiʻi Technology Development Corporation; Celeste Connors of East-West Center; Gregg Oishi of Kuakini Health Systems; Joshua Knisley and Daniel Sepulveda of Veterans Assn of Real Estate Professionals (VAREP)… (1/2)

I stepped out of Appropriations to meet with Hawai’i Health and Harm Reduction Center and Gregory House visitors on critical federal programs supporting their incredible service to communities living with HIV/AIDS, hepatitis and other health challenges as well as facing homelessness, substance abuse, mental illness and poverty.

Despite including many of my requests especially on Native Hawaiian efforts, I couldn’t support my majority Appropriations colleagues’ Labor/Education/Health/Human Services proposal slashing public education, workforce development, public health and other critical programs with so many real-world negative effects. https://t.co/cROiroWhs5

Day 9 of a completely avoidable and fixable federal shutdown  and House Republican leadership has cancelled another full week of voting in DC at which we could easily and quickly pass a bipartisan solution to avert a health care crisis for tens of millions of American and reopen government. So I kept going with my Walk Story Round 3, Day 3 thru my communities, this one in industrial Kalihi Kai where the cost of doing business especially due to the administration’s destructive trade/tariff policy is tops. Also walked Democrat, Republican and Homerule Streets so maybe a sign of a breakthrough in DC.
A quick report from Capitol Hill on the reality of what it’s going to take to end this unnecessary and solvable federal health care/funding shutdown. https://t.co/LzztUvmr2J

Still in DC awaiting the Speaker calling the U.S. House back into session (which he has refused to do for 40 full days now) to contribute to the bipartisan solution which is the only way out of the shutdown/health care crisis. Joined colleagues on two letters to the administration demanding that (1) $5 billion in available Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) contingency funds be released to continue food assistance to some 165,000 Hawai’i residents, and (2) the threat that federal workers will (illegally) not be paid back pay once the shutdown be fully retracted.

Back to DC again to help end this shutdown, but for the 48th day now the Speaker refuses to bring the House back into session to get this done and back to work. What are they so afraid of? That we might actually solve this funding/health care/nutrition assistance crisis and turn back to our many other challenges?

As we strive to end this shutdown/health care crisis, I joined our Hawai’i Foodbank’s great volunteers at a special food distribution for our veterans, military and federal employees at Keehi Lagoon Memorial Park, with over 550 families coming thru for assistance. https://t.co/iTS697Eb3a

Months of behind-the-scenes hard work with House colleagues thru the federal shutdown and beyond to solve the impending healthcare crisis for tens of million of Americans has resulted in 35 of us endorsing our Commonground 2025 – A Bipartisan Health Care Framework to advance a real solution that could pass a divided Congress: https://t.co/Sx2EfmnCDq
